data.description:
# Colour of service businesses

## Problem statement

Service businesses render in a dark purple that is visually indistinguishable
from the flat purple face used by every upgrade card, so the two card families
read as the same thing at a glance on the street and in hand. At the same
time, an upgrade card carries no information about *what* it upgrades: all 39
upgrade cards share one uniform purple face regardless of the business they
apply to.

## Users

- **Main Street player** (primary) — scanning their hand and the market needs
  to distinguish a service business from an upgrade card instantly, and to see
  which family of business an upgrade belongs to without reading its title.
  - *As a player, I want service businesses in a colour no other card family
    uses, so I never mistake a service business for an upgrade card.*
  - *As a player, I want each upgrade card to show the colour of the business
    family it upgrades, so I can pick a relevant upgrade from my hand without
    reading every title.*

- **Colour-blind player** — the distinction must not rely on hue alone; the
  checkered pattern is itself a non-colour cue, and the upgrade card keeps its
  title and "for <Business>" target text.

## Existing state

- Synergy-type card faces are coloured from two parallel palettes:
  `CARD_FACE_PALETTE` (dark faces, `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and the
  bright `synergyColor` accent palette. The static Node generator
  (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) duplicates both; an
  existing test asserts the two copies of the face palette agree
  (MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4).
- Service currently holds dark purple `#6A1B9A` (face) / `0x9B59B6` (accent).
- Upgrade cards are flat purple: background `#6B4C9A`, accent `#9B59B6`,
  rendered by `generateUpgradeCardSvg` / `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and by
  `cardColorScheme` / the family branch in the `.mjs` generator.
- 39 upgrade rows in `src/card-data.csv` carry a `targetBusiness` name but no
  synergy column of their own; synergy must be resolved by looking the target
  name up among business **and** community-space rows (6 targets are community
  spaces: Community Garden, Health Kiosk, Library, Park, Playground, Town
  Fountain).
- 9 businesses are bridge cards with two synergy types; 11 upgrade rows target
  them (Cafe, Food Truck, Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga
  Studio, Teahouse).

## Desired change

1. **New service colour.** Replace Service's palette entries with a pink /
   magenta that no other synergy type uses, in **both** palettes (face and
   accent) and in **both** copies (TypeScript and the `.mjs` duplicate), so the
   palette-agreement test still passes.
2. **Checkered upgrade faces.** Upgrade card faces become a checkerboard of
   violet and the synergy colour of the business the upgrade targets, instead
   of the current flat purple.
3. **Bridge targets use both colours.** When the upgrade targets a card with
   two synergy types, the checkerboard uses both synergy colours (with violet
   in the remaining squares).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Service synergy type's face colour is a pink/magenta distinct from
      every other synergy colour, applied in `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`
      (`src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and its `.mjs` duplicate
      (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`); the existing
      TS/mjs palette-agreement test passes unchanged in intent.
- [ ] The bright Service accent colour (`synergyColor`) is updated to the
      matching pink/magenta family so icons, header tint and art backing stay
      consistent (the `expanded-card-pool` assertion is updated to the new
      value).
- [ ] A generated upgrade card face renders as a checkerboard of violet and
      the target's synergy colour, for both the runtime generator
      (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` / `generateUpgradeCardSvg`) and the static
      `.mjs` generator, with both paths producing the same pattern.
- [ ] An upgrade targeting a single-synergy business yields a two-colour
      checkerboard (violet + that synergy colour).
- [ ] An upgrade targeting a bridge business (two synergy types) yields all
      three colours: violet plus **both** synergy colours.
- [ ] An upgrade whose target synergy cannot be resolved (unknown or missing
      target) degrades safely to the existing flat purple face and never
      throws.
- [ ] Upgrade cards remain legible: title, "for <Business>" target text, cost
      badge and art stay readable over the checkerboard (existing contrast
      expectations in the SVG tests are preserved).
- [ ] New unit tests cover: the new service colour, single-synergy
      checkerboard, bridge-target three-colour checkerboard, unresolvable
      target fallback, and TS/mjs pattern agreement.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The static Node generator runs outside the TS build and cannot import
  TypeScript modules, so any palette or resolver change must be duplicated
  there and kept in agreement (existing project pattern).
- Upgrade synergy colour must be **derived**, not added as a new CSV column:
  `targetBusiness` is the only link today, and adding data columns would
  invalidate CSV checksums and pack fixtures.
- Upgrade **card** faces change only. The in-game board upgrade accent (the
  gold corner shard on an upgraded business, `UpgradeOverlaySpec`) and the
  owner-coloured seat border are out of scope — they are a separate visual
  language and were deliberately settled by MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF.
- Card faces must remain readable at the reduced hand/stacked scale (the art
  zone and text column must not be masked by the pattern).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — new Service entry in `synergyColor` and
  `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`; likely the natural home for a pure
  `upgradeFaceBackground(targetSynergyTypes)`-style resolver.
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — duplicated palettes plus
  the `upgrade` family branch in `cardColorScheme`; mirror the checkerboard and
  the new service colour.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `generateUpgradeCardSvg`,
  `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` (upgrade branch) and `cardColorScheme`; emit the
  checkerboard rect group (mirroring the existing `cardFaceSplitSvg` approach,
  possibly generalised into a checker tile helper).
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` — re-export any new resolver alongside
  `cardFaceBackground`.
- `src/card-data.csv` — read-only reference: `targetBusiness` values are the
  lookup keys; no schema change expected.
- `tests/main-street/mjs-svg-generator.test.ts` — palette-agreement and static
  render-path tests; extend for the checkerboard.
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — runtime SVG generator tests;
  add upgrade-face cases.
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — asserts the Service accent
  value; update to the new colour.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4 — Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge
  cards)** (completed) — established `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`, `cardFaceBackground`
  and the TS/mjs palette-agreement test this item builds on.
- **MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF — Identify different AI players** (completed) — moved
  upgrade state to the owner-coloured border + top-left accent; constrains the
  board visual language this item must not disturb.
- **MS-0MVZC5V6L001OOXN — Upgrade highlights should only be the current
  player's businesses** (completed) — upgrade targeting/placement rendering;
  related to how upgrade cards are presented.
- **MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38 — shader-style upgrade accent remediation** — the
  board-level gold upgrade shard; explicitly out of scope here (Q2 = A).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: palette collision.** Pink must be checked against the seat-colour
  palette (`MainStreetSeatColours`) — seat colours identify *owners*, synergy
  colours identify *card families*; a near-identical pink could blur that.
  Mitigation: pick a pink distinguishable from the seat palette and note the
  choice in comments.
- **Risk: legibility at small scale.** A checkerboard under the 64×64 art zone
  and the text column may reduce contrast. Mitigation: keep the pattern
  behind the existing translucent overlays, keep tile contrast modest, and
  assert legibility in the SVG tests.
- **Risk: colour as sole cue.** Mitigation: the pattern itself is a non-colour
  cue, and the title plus "for <Business>" line remain.
- **Risk: two copy drift.** The TS and `.mjs` generators can diverge silently.
  Mitigation: extend the existing agreement test to the checkerboard geometry
  and colours.
- **Risk: scope creep.** A general "cards show their family colour" refactor,
  a redesign of the board upgrade accent, or adding a `targetSynergy` CSV
  column are all out of scope — record as separate work items if raised.
- **Assumption:** "violet" for the retained checkerboard colour means the
  existing upgrade family purple (`#6B4C9A`); the request says
  "the current colour and the colour of the type of business they upgrade".
- **Assumption:** bridge targets show both synergy colours because the
  producer explicitly chose option B in the intake interview.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which colour should Service businesses become?** (asked because the
  brief said "change the service business" without naming a colour) —
  Answer (producer, interactive reply): **(a) Pink/magenta** (`#AD1457` /
  `#C2185B` family), chosen to be distinct from every other synergy hue.

- **Q: Where should the checkered upgrade pattern apply?** — Answer (producer,
  interactive reply): **(a) Upgrade card faces only** — the market/hand card
  face changes; the in-game board upgrade accent stays as-is.

- **Q: For upgrades targeting a bridge business with two synergy types, which
  colour does the checkerboard use?** — Answer (producer, interactive reply):
  **(b) Both colours** — the checkerboard uses violet plus both synergy
  colours.

- **Q: (research, no producer input needed) Do upgrade rows carry a synergy
  column?** — Answer: no; all 39 upgrade rows have an empty `targetSynergy`.
  Synergy must be resolved from `targetBusiness` against the business and
  community-space rows. Source: `src/card-data.csv`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MV76HVE4007AOO0** – Allow drag and drop of upgrades from hand to card (completed)
- **MS-0MVZC5V6L001OOXN** – Upgarde highlights should only be the current players businesses (completed)
- **MS-0MV5VOIV40020KXT** – Smarter AI hand acquisition: gate expensive businesses and untargeted upgrades (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: also, business, businesses, change, colour, current, make, pattern, service, they, type, upgrade, upgrades
- `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — matched: also, business, businesses, change, colour, current, make, pattern, service, they, type, upgrade, upgrades
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: also, business, businesses, change, colour, current, make, pattern, they, type, upgrade, upgrades

data.description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A business-staff member (has `employedAtSlot`) holding a management-company-scope skill (Brand Ambassador, Cost Cutter, Negotiator, any incident-mitigation skill, or Town Gossip) produces **no** player- or street-scope effect.
- The test asserts that `getEmployedSpecializationSkills` and `getEmployedSpecializationSkillsForBusiness` return the skill but the effect folds (income, reputation, ongoing-cost, incident, refresh discount) are zero for that skill.
- Tests cover each management-company skill class held by business staff: at least one from incident-mitigation, one from cost-reduction (MC-scope), and Brand Ambassador (reputation multiplier on events).
data.title: Test: scope gate blocks business-staff holding management-company skills

data.description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Business staff (those with `employedAtSlot`) draw only business-scope skills from the assignment pool.
- The test creates a seeded RNG, simulates the type-consistent assignment path for business staff, and asserts that no management-company-scope skill ID appears in the result.
- Covers each business-scope skill category: income-boost, cost-reduction (business: Operations Manager), reputation-boost (business-scope subset).
data.title: Test: type-consistent assignment (business staff draw business-scope skills only)
